examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.note: To name or address someone. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'зывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to call; to name', paired with 'назвать'.

To assign a title. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'зывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to call; to name', paired with 'назвать'.

examples.trans: Call me simply Lev from now on.

examples.text: А вы называйте меня просто Вика.
examples.trans: And you call me simply Vika.

examples.text: Они называют себя лучшим рестораном города.
examples.trans: They call themselves the best restaurant in town.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: По объявлению = through an ad. Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ъявление'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'advertisement, notice, announcement' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I found the job through an ad.
A notice is hanging on the door.

examples.text: По объявлению. Девочка — сирота, у неё трагедия.
examples.trans: Through an ad. The girl is an orphan, she has a tragedy.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.
перестань(те)! = stop it!, oh come on!

examples.text: Иначе я перестану давать тебе деньги!
examples.trans: Otherwise I'll stop giving you money!

examples.text: Приезжай сейчас! Иначе я перестану давать тебе деньги!
examples.trans: Come over right now! Otherwise I'll stop giving you money!

meanings.note: Person who wins. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'бедитель'). Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'winner' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The name of the grand winner.

examples.text: Перед тем, как я объявлю победителя, внимание!
examples.trans: Before I announce the winner, your attention!

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get, to receive', paired with 'получать'.

examples.text: А кто их получит? Те, кто сидит повыше?
examples.trans: And who will get it? The people who sit higher up?

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'bonus, prize, reward' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You are due a state bonus.

examples.text: В конце года работники получили премию.
examples.trans: At the end of the year the workers received a bonus.

examples.text: И небольшую государственную премию за помощь.
examples.trans: And a modest state bonus for your help.

meanings.en: to think up, to invent, to make up
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'думывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to think up, to invent', paired with 'придумать'.

examples.trans: And what is there to think up?
There's no need to make anything up.

examples.text: А что тут придумывать? Всё, приехали, это финиш!
examples.trans: And what is there to think up? That's it, we've arrived, this is the finish!

meanings.note: Literally 'until the meeting'. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'видание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting; date' in everyday Russian.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'езонный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('seasonal').

examples.trans: The chef is preparing a seasonal dish.

examples.text: Ты обещал новое сезонное блюдо, Виктор.
examples.trans: You promised a new seasonal dish, Viktor.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.trans: You can see it at once.
